title: Capitalism

definition.text: An economic system built on private ownership of the means of production, run to obtain profit.

facts.text: Its constituent elements are private property, profit motive, capital accumulation, competitive markets, commodification, wage labor, and an emphasis on innovation and economic growth.
Economic growth is a characteristic tendency of capitalist economies, which also swing through business cycles of expansion and recession.
Capital accumulation is central: financial capital is invested for profit, then reinvested in further production in a continuous process.
Eco-capitalism holds that natural capital, ecosystems with ecological yield, underlies all wealth, so governments should use market instruments such as a carbon tax against environmental problems.
Sustainable capitalism is a conceptual form built on sustainable practices that reduce externalities; the page notes that a capitalist economy must expand to survive and find new markets.

contested_note: There is no universally agreed definition of capitalism, and it is unclear whether it describes a whole society or only elements of one.

definition.text: An economic system in which investment, production and the allocation of capital goods follow economy-wide plans.

facts.text: Planning can be centralized, decentralized, participatory or Soviet-type; it contrasts with market economies, where autonomous firms decide production, pricing and investment.

Critics argue planners cannot detect consumer preferences, shortages and surpluses accurately enough; Mises and Hayek described this as the economic calculation problem and the local knowledge problem.
Supporters argue the state can direct land, labor and capital to its objectives; in the 1930s Soviet Union private consumption was forced down from 80% to 50% of gross national income.
Market economies using indicative planning are called mixed economies or planned market economies.
